stem.en: In the shoe-size data of 27 students, 3 students wear size 3, 9 wear size 4, 10 wear size 5, 4 wear size 6 and 1 wears size 7. How many students wear size 5?

why.en: 9 is the number of students wearing size 4.
27 is the total number of students.

stem.en: How many of those 27 students wear a shoe size larger than 4?

why.en: This counts only size 5 and leaves out sizes 6 and 7.
You may have added 10 + 1 + 1; size 6 has 4 students.

explanation.en: Add the students for sizes 5, 6 and 7: 10 + 4 + 1 = 15.

stem.en: In a pictograph one symbol stands for 10 children. How many children do 3 and a half symbols stand for?

why.en: A half symbol is 5 children, not 10.
You forgot to multiply by the key of 10.

explanation.en: 3 symbols are 30 children and a half symbol is 5 children, so 35.

stem.en: Why do we choose a scale before drawing a bar graph?

text.en: So that the bars fit on the paper and are easy to mark and read
To make the graph more colourful

whyWrong.en: Colour is a decoration; the scale decides the bar length.

text.en: So that we do not need to label the graph

whyWrong.en: Every graph still needs a title and labels.

explanation.en: The scale tells how many items one unit of bar length stands for.

stem.en: In tally marks, the fifth mark is drawn across the previous four marks.

explanation.en: Tally marks are grouped in fives: four straight lines and a fifth line crossing them.

stem.en: With a scale of 1 unit = 10 runs, how many units high is the bar for 90 runs?

why.en: That would be the bar for a scale of 1 unit = 1 run.
10 is the number of runs for one unit, not the bar height.

stem.en: The population of India was 36 crores in 1951 and 102 crores in 2001. By how many crores did it grow?

why.en: 138 is the sum of 36 and 102; growth needs subtraction.
54 is the population in 1971, not the growth between 1951 and 2001.

stem.en: Which graph is best to show the heights of the tallest mountains on the continents?

whyWrong.en: Heights go upward, so vertical bars give the natural picture.
A tally table cannot compare the heights at a glance.

explanation.en: Heights are measured upward from the ground, so columns suit them.

stem.en: In the sweets data the frequencies are 6, 9, 13, 3 and 7. How many students answered in all?

why.en: 13 is only the number who chose gujiya.
Check the addition; the total is 38.

stem.en: In the same sweets data, how many more students chose gujiya than barfi?

why.en: 3 is the number who chose barfi.

explanation.en: Gujiya has 13 and barfi has 3, and 13 - 3 = 10.
